To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) relative dispersion (the standard deviation divided by the mean radius of droplet size distributions) is an important parameter that controls the first aerosol–cloud interaction, (ii) climate models tend to underestimate relative dispersion, and (iii) this underestimation of relative dispersion is the main reason for the underestimation of aerosol‐induced radiative forcing in current climate models.
the dispersion bias in climate models is likely near its theoretical maximum for ambient clouds, and that this bias can be comparable in magnitude to the warming caused from doubling CO2.
